messages:
sam: Quick sync — new customer wants Redwood Private (VPC) deployed using their own AWS account CMK for both control-plane secrets and data-plane DEK wrapping. I want to confirm the least-privileged policy and a safe rotation plan.

jaya: Do we plan to assume a role in their account or ask them to add our control-plane role to the key policy? pros/cons? :thinking_face:

sam: Prefer key-policy allow + condition on SourceAccount + principal ARN for the control-plane role. Simpler for KMS semantics (cross-account Decrypt + GenerateDataKey). If they don't want that, we can use an assume-role flow but key policy still needs to reference the principal.

maria: For data-plane (on-prem/private workers) we should avoid giving broad Decrypt perms. Idea: control-plane issues encrypted DEKs (GenerateDataKey) and stores ciphertext. Workers call KMS:Decrypt on ciphertext only when they need plaintext. That reduces blast radius.

sam: Agreed. Minimal permissions: control-plane role -> [kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Encrypt, kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:DescribeKey]. data-plane node role -> [kms:Decrypt, kms:DescribeKey] for the CMK alias.

lee: Can you paste an example key policy snippet we can show the customer?

sam: Sure — here's a small example to propose (customer CMK key policy):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Id": "key-default-1",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDCUSTOMERACCOUNT:role/redwood-controlplane-prod"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:SourceAccount": "REDCUSTOMERACCOUNT"}}
    }
  ]
}
```

jaya: We should call out external-id if customers want extra protection when we have cross-account assume-role flows. Also mention they can narrow Principal to the specific role ARN.

maria: Rotation concerns — if the CMK is rotated (customer enables automatic rotation or manually rotates), we'll need to rewrap all stored DEKs with the new CMK. That can be expensive; propose a background rewrap job that reads ciphertext_DEK -> ReEncrypt to new CMK -> write back atomically. ReEncrypt is the safe atomic KMS operation for this.

sam: Right. Plan: 1) customer enables rotation on CMK OR they rotate manually. 2) schedule immediate ReEncrypt rewrap job for all DEK ciphertexts with retry/backoff. 3) keep DEK versioning in metadata so we can fallback if a rewrap fails.

lee: Any required IAM changes for the rewrap job? I assume control-plane needs kms:ReEncryptFrom and kms:ReEncryptTo actions depending on source/destination key ARNs.

sam: Good catch — yes, if rewrapping between two CMKs (e.g., old->new alias), we need kms:ReEncryptFrom & kms:ReEncryptTo for the involved key ARNs or allow kms:ReEncrypt*. If the customer rotates the same CMK (auto-rotate), ReEncrypt still uses the key id but permissions remain same.

maria: Audit logging: ensure CloudTrail is configured in the customer's account for KMS events. We should add an alert rule in Redwood Console to detect unexpected kms:Decrypt calls from IPs/roles outside expected ranges or spikes in Decrypt calls after onboarding. Tie that to our incident playbook.

kms-bot: Reminder: CloudTrail will log KMS events but Decrypt payloads are not in logs. Use CloudTrail + Athena for quick queries on eventName = "Decrypt" and errorCode filters.

jaya: What about grants vs key policy? Grants short-lived might be useful for bursty worker pods that need temporary Decrypt rights without modifying key policy. Thoughts?

sam: Grants are useful for ephemeral access (e.g., AWS account A creates grant for a role/instance). But for predictable control-plane role across accounts, key policy + IAM is simpler and easier for auditing. For ephemeral pods we can create grants with RetireGrant when done. Be careful: grants can complicate rotation (you may need to retire grants).

maria: Vulnerability triage note — if a worker's role is compromised, both grants and key-policy permissions allow decryption. So mitigate by short-lived credentials, pod RBAC, and requiring network-level restrictions for the data-plane. We'll add a quarterly tabletop for KMS compromise scenarios.

lee: Downtime during rewrap?

sam: No planned downtime. We'll implement rewrap as read-modify-write with new ciphertext version and fallbacks. We plan to keep old ciphertext for a configurable grace period until all nodes pick up new DEK versions. That reduces risk.

jaya: Next steps for ops: 1) draft customer-facing onboarding doc (policy snippet + required ARNs + CloudTrail checklist). 2) implement rewrap job and DEK versioning. 3) update RBAC and run a staging test with a test account.

maria: I'll own the onboarding doc and the audit playbook updates.

sam: I'll prototype the rewrap job and a small test harness. Lee, can you run the staging test next week?

lee: Yep, adding to my calendar.

maria: Thanks — I'll ping legal for wording on key custody and rotation SLAs. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks team. If anyone hits a permissions error during staging, paste the kms error + request ID here and kms-bot will give quick lookup tips.

kms-bot: Tip: common error "AccessDeniedException" when cross-account — check key policy principal + aws:SourceAccount condition and IAM role ARN match.

lee: ack :white_check_mark:
